extracted_items.text: ## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Revised readiness posture after owner-doc and storage passes
Targeted docs: working_ledger.md, storage-plan.md, UI_Command_Catalog.md, Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md, human-in-the-loop.md, Executor_Protocol.md

Remaining work splits into: still-structural gaps (missing canonical model/owner decisions), spec-integrity failures (docs promise canon that does not exist or conflicts), plain reconciliation cleanup (stable direction, retargeting consumers)

Still-structural gaps blocking reconciliation: TierContext successor ownership, blocked/approval identity minting and scope (blocked_sequence, approval scope key, request/block bridge), missing storage families for runtime-artifact indexing and worktree/lane lifecycle, durable lineage bridges from planning/wizard/validation into launched execution

Spec-integrity failures: ghost command IDs, missing catalog rows for referenced commands, missing runtime-artifact schema family / storage registration, duplicated executor canon, missing advertised sections and dead glossary references

Reconciliation cleanup bucket: update stale tier-era consumers, align requested/effective/account/runtime identity displays, move surfaces to canonical route payloads and runtime actions, tab/layout/help/glossary cleanup, lane/worktree/package/seam-aware wording

Working classification — still needs research: execution-unit context owner and minimum field contract; blocked approval identity/scope and blocked_sequence minting; durable storage for runtime-artifact indexing/projection and worktree/lane lifecycle; validation/wizard/interview lineage bridge into launched execution

Must-fix before reconciliation: command/catalog ghost IDs and missing owner rows; payload/schema-owner triangle for runtime artifacts; duplicated/contradictory executor and HITL canon; glossary/crosswalk/TOC dead references and missing advertised sections

Primarily reconciliation once settled: Orchestrator tab/page retargeting, Source Control vs Orchestrator cleanup, help/glossary expansion, stale consumer-doc identity cleanup, concern/search/attention/project-summary alignment
Not safe to call ready_for_reconciliation until structural owner gaps are assigned/resolved and dangerous spec-integrity failures are concrete reconciliation targets rather than live ambiguity

Do-not-forget: "not ready" means small set of structural owner gaps plus hard SSOT integrity failures; spec-integrity failures are not fresh design space but still block reconciliation; work item stays active with center shifting to owner-hardening
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Blocked episode ownership and startup-recovery handshake
Targeted docs: Contracts_V0.md, Executor_Protocol.md, human-in-the-loop.md, storage-plan.md, Decision_Policy.md, UI_Command_Catalog.md

Canonical blocked field family: node.blocked/node.unblocked, blocked_reason_code, blocked_sequence, allowed_action_ids[], node.prerequisite_resolved, wake_reason = approval_resolved | clarification_resolved | auth_recovered | startup_recovered | ...

Missing ownership semantics: who mints blocked_sequence; when new blocked episode vs update; request_id competes with blocked_sequence in HITL/storage; startup_recovered not tied to concrete blocked-episode restoration rule
blocked_sequence owned by runtime scheduler/executor, not UI/HITL/chat/storage; monotonic per { run_id, node_id }, starts at 1, increments only on non-blocked → new blocked episode transition

Blocked episode canonical unit for: approval waiting, clarification waiting, auth/prerequisite waiting, permission/FileSafe/external-side-effect block, worktree conflict/dirty-worktree block; same blocked_sequence when updating metadata for same unresolved prerequisite

blocked_sequence canonical; request_id child/compatibility for approval UX/history; waiting_approval episode first-class in runtime/state; request_id maps 1:1 to { run_id, node_id, blocked_sequence }; request_id must never be only durable key for recovery/mutation; approval commands route by blocked episode identity

Startup recovery: restore unresolved blocked episodes from canonical records; scheduler emits startup_recovered pass; does not mint new episodes; stale_historical attempt if cannot resume; resolve/unblock explicitly if prerequisite satisfied externally

storage-plan still publishes HITL events with allowed_actions and tier-local request payloads while runtime blocked projections use blocked_sequence and allowed_action_ids[]; UI_Command_Catalog routes by blocked_sequence but graph-local HITL uses request_id; Decision_Policy does not own minting or same-episode vs new-episode; Executor_Protocol names startup_recovered but weak restore handshake risks silent block-loss or accidental reminting

Joint owners Executor_Protocol + Contracts_V0 for blocked_sequence minting, blocked-episode lifecycle, startup-recovery handshake; subordinate request_id to blocked-episode identity; align storage on allowed_action_ids/blocked_sequence/runtime routing; deterministic same-episode vs new-episode rule in Decision_Policy or Executor_Protocol
Do-not-forget blocked seam: resolvable via ownership not new concepts; blocked_sequence runtime-owned; startup recovery rehydrates unresolved episodes not fresh opportunistic ones
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Opus owner-doc tranche synthesis

Owner-doc tranche: Commands_System, Wiring_Matrix, UI_Wiring_Rules, Project_Output_Artifacts, Glossary, FileManager, Crosswalk, Decision_Policy, Run_Modes, Progression_Gates, newtools, assistant-memory-subsystem; contradiction checks against UI_Command_Catalog, assistant-chat-design, Contracts_V0, storage-plan, Orchestrator_Page, WorktreeGitImprovement, Permissions_System, Tools

Command/wiring: Commands_System AC contradiction on reserved slash-command overrides vs assistant-chat-design/UI_Command_Catalog; cmd.chat.run_user_command defined but not in catalog; Wiring_Matrix ghost IDs (cmd.chat.branch_from_restore, cmd.orchestrator.switch_tab); UI_Wiring_Rules cannot express freshness/health, permission gating, dynamic allowed_action_ids[], mutation safety — GATE-010 cannot verify runtime contracts
newtools introduces ghost cmd.orchestrator.preview_*, build_run, CustomHeadlessTool ToolID without catalog/tool/permission registration

Artifact/lineage holes: Project_Output_Artifacts under-keyed vs EventRecord/runtime (missing project/thread/run/attempt/account, pass_verdict vs wizard, interview glossary/evidence types vs package SSOT); FileManager path-only open vs runtime-identity addendum; assistant-memory-subsystem memory events/AutoRunBoundary/attention_required persistence/HITL CTA commands unregistered in storage-plan or catalog

Glossary dead forward refs (Overseer), missing rewrite vocabulary (execution_role, operational_identity, projection_freshness/health, attention item, concern); Crosswalk structurally broken, missing rewrite-era owners; Decision_Policy leaves blocked_sequence minting, startup recovery, retry/remediation counters, runtime blocked escalation, ready_since_utc unowned; Run_Modes three incompatible isolation models; Progression_Gates planning-centric, no formal gates for concern/corroboration/promotion/runtime blocked/governance

Highest-risk impacted: UI_Command_Catalog (ghost-ID dependents), Commands_System (AC + uncataloged IDs), Project_Output_Artifacts (thin lineage), FileManager (cannot open by runtime identity), Glossary (missing definitions)

Crosswalk structurally unreliable as boundary map during rewrite ownership disputes; Decision_Policy missing deterministic policies executor/storage assume; newtools and assistant-memory-subsystem invent commands/events faster than canonical owners register

Command/wiring stack: multiple hard ghost-ID failures; owner docs claim EventRecord alignment but omit project/thread/run/attempt/account in schemas; rewrite governance terms lack glossary owner while docs point there; Crosswalk and Progression Gates structural integrity issues make them unreliable authorities

Reconcile slash-command override policy; register real cmd.chat.* / cmd.orchestrator.* before more wiring; upgrade Project_Output_Artifacts and neighbors for canonical lineage; FileManager runtime-identity open path; promote Glossary vocabulary and fix dead refs; repair Crosswalk/Progression Gates; register memory/live-preview/build events in storage/tool/command owners

Do-not-forget: cmd.chat.run_user_command only in Commands_System; cmd.orchestrator.switch_tab and cmd.chat.branch_from_restore referenced without catalog; Project_Output_Artifacts vs interview glossary/evidence types; Overseer dead glossary ref; FileManager OpenFile path shape cannot satisfy runtime-identity addendum without resolution layer
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Execution-context owner split and `TierContext` replacement
Targeted docs: Prompt_Pipeline.md, storage-plan.md, Executor_Protocol.md, orchestrator-subagent-integration.md

Owner split: Prompt_Pipeline owns effective-resolution record (requested/effective persona/platform/model/auth/account + selection metadata); storage-plan owns attempt_record, tier_runtime_record, blocked_projection, usage_record; orchestrator-subagent-integration embeds TierContext mixing decomposition/view identity, workspace heuristics, execution-state hints, canonical runtime identity

Recommended split: Prompt_Pipeline keeps effective-resolution field family; storage-plan persistence/projection; Executor_Protocol minimum execution-scoped context for scheduler/executor correctness; orchestrator-subagent-integration consumes canonical context by reference, keeps only local selection/decomposition helpers

Replacement model: canonical execution_unit_context; optional decomposition_context or selection_context — TierContext may remain tier-shaped only for derived selection heuristics, not canonical runtime context

execution_unit_context minimum shape: identity/lineage (project_id, run_id, thread_id?, feature_seam_id?, work_package_id?, node_id, attempt_id?, blocked_sequence?, replan_generation); execution ownership (execution_role, scheduler_lane, manual_priority?, safe_point_id?, remediation refs); workspace/isolation (lane_id?, worktree_id?, workspace_ref, snapshot_ref?); requested/effective runtime identity fields; runtime state hooks (blocked_reason_code?, allowed_action_ids[]?, failure_class?, permission_snapshot_id?, provider_attempt_ref?)

decomposition_context/selection_context: tier/view identity (tier_type, tier_id, titles); heuristic inputs only (language, framework, domain, subtask_focus, has_errors, needs_testing, error_patterns, parent_subagents) — allowed tier-shaped if policy wants selectors, not canonical runtime
Impacted: orchestrator-subagent-integration, Executor_Protocol, storage-plan, Prompt_Pipeline; downstream Orchestrator_Page, Run_Graph_View, human-in-the-loop, Runtime_Artifacts_Panel

storage-plan publishes attempt_record and tier_runtime_record but tier_runtime_record still tier-shaped progress; Prompt_Pipeline strong effective-resolution duplicated thinly on TierContext; orchestrator-subagent-integration constructs TierContext without clear run/node/attempt/lane identity; Executor_Protocol node-native but lacks explicit execution-context contract at dispatch

Introduce execution_unit_context canonical; TierContext derived/compatibility-only; recast tier_runtime_record as current-view overlay; refactor orchestrator-subagent-integration to consume execution-unit refs + smaller selection object

Do-not-forget execution context: mostly ownership cleanup; highest-risk triplicate is requested/effective identity in prompt pipeline, storage, tier context; TierContext if it survives is derived helper not canonical runtime owner
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - `tier_runtime_record` as derived overlay and downstream surface drift
Targeted docs: Run_Graph_View.md, Orchestrator_Page.md, human-in-the-loop.md, spot-checks storage-plan.md

Surfaces still tier-shaped vs runtime/storage: Run_Graph_View uses tier_id for output/verification/usage/copy/open/event drill-in; Orchestrator_Page Progress/Tiers/Node Graph with TierChanged, tier_id, tier-scoped widgets; human-in-the-loop split request_id+tier vs blocked_reason_code+blocked_sequence; surfaces behave as if tier_runtime_record canonical though attempt_record + blocked hold truth

tier_runtime_record may survive only as derived current-view/runtime-overlay projection: visible progress for tier-shaped UI grouping, latest attempt/blocked pointer, tab badges — not canonical for execution identity, retry lineage, approval/recovery targeting, usage truth

Canonical mutation and audit route by run_id, node_id, attempt_id?, blocked_sequence?; tier surfaces may display/group by tier_id but resolve through pointers to canonical execution objects, not tier_id as durable execution key
Impacted: Run_Graph_View, Orchestrator_Page, human-in-the-loop, storage-plan, Runtime_Artifacts_Panel

Run_Graph_View node graph but tier_id joins for Usage/Output; Orchestrator_Page tab 2 Tiers vs Seams direction; human-in-the-loop approval state request_id+tier_id+tier_type vs blocked-episode model; evidence/terminal routing still tier-keyed — wrong under multi-attempt/blocked/graph generations

Keep tier_runtime_record as compatibility overlay explicit in storage-plan; surface specs carry pointers to canonical execution objects; retarget Run Graph and Usage to node_id/attempt_id; HITL around blocked-episode first, tier as metadata

Do-not-forget surface drift: tier_id may remain human-readable grouping but must stop acting as canonical execution correlation key; high-risk pages Orchestrator_Page, Run_Graph_View, human-in-the-loop
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Concrete executor-facing `execution_unit_context` field contract
Targeted docs: Contracts_V0.md, Prompt_Pipeline.md, Executor_Protocol.md, storage-plan.md, spot-checks orchestrator-subagent-integration.md

Field family split across Contracts_V0 (runtime event packets), Prompt_Pipeline (immutable handoff at attempt start), storage-plan (attempt_record, blocked_projection); missing executor-facing mandatory vs optional statement

execution_unit_context = union of immutable attempt handoff identity, active blocked/recovery/runtime gating anchors, workspace/isolation refs — strict enough for dispatch, worker spawn, safe-point, retry/remediation, approval targeting, UI audit
Mandatory dispatch identity for any dispatched attempt: run_id, node_id, attempt_id, scheduler_pass_id, replan_generation, execution_role
Mandatory runtime lineage/recovery anchors when applicable: safe_point_id?, remediation_root_id?, remediation_parent_attempt_id?, blocked_sequence?, failure_class?, blocked_reason_code?

Mandatory requested/effective snapshots by reference for provider-executed attempts: persona/model/permission snapshot refs, requested_auth_mode?, effective_auth_mode?, requested_account_policy?, effective_account_id?, account_switch_reason?
Mandatory workspace/side-effect anchors when mutation-capable: mutation_capable, lane_id?, worktree_id?, workspace_ref, provider_attempt_ref?
Optional disclosure: thread_id?, feature_seam_id?, work_package_id?, scheduler_lane, manual_priority?, allowed_action_ids[]?, operational_identity?, effective_project_id?

execution_unit_context: strict mandatory core for executor correctness, conditional blocked/remediation family, disclosure family for UI/audit; attempt.started and immutable handoff bundle should be isomorphically projectable

Contracts_V0 attempt.started strong but omits execution_role; Prompt_Pipeline handoff omits some blocked/recovery fields for resumed flows; storage-plan tier_runtime_record next to attempt_record risks consumers binding to tier projection; EventEnvelopeV1 run_id/thread_id only "should" — executor dispatch must not inherit that looseness

Add execution_unit_context section to Executor_Protocol; add execution_role to Contracts_V0 attempt packet; align handoff bundle with attempt.started; tier surfaces consume pointers not tier_id reconstruction

Do-not-forget executor contract: normalization across owners not greenfield; most important missing field execution_role; invariants: handoff immutable, attempt.started canonical start packet, blocked/recovery conditional first-class
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Placement of `execution_role` and `operational_identity`
Targeted docs: Multi-Account.md, Contracts_V0.md, storage-plan.md, Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md, usage-feature.md, spot-checks Orchestrator_Page.md

Provider/account identity shared across roles but does not explain what actor was doing; effective_provider_identity/provider_identity/effective_project_id are disclosure-only — wrong place for actor role or side-effect target
orchestrator.receipt.{run_id}.{attempt_id} bridges GitHub workflow, Docker, Kubernetes, worktree/branch — closer to operational_identity than persona snapshot

execution_role in canonical runtime attempt/dispatch packet family (handoff, attempt.started, attempt_record, usage/worker projections); operational_identity in operational bridge (attempt_record when side effects, receipts, runtime artifacts/tool traces, history inspectors)

execution_role: what kind of actor/responsibility (assistant, interviewer, builder, overseers, node worker, verifier, corroborator, recovery); operational_identity: external side-effect target (GitHub org/repo/workflow, Docker, K8s, etc.) — do not collapse with provider account

Minimum contract: add execution_role to immutable handoff, attempt.started, attempt_record, worker inspectors; add operational_identity? to attempt_record, receipt/bridge records, tool.invoked/denied/artifact when side effects; keep effective_provider_identity/provider_identity as provider-native disclosure only, never actor-role or external-target identity
Impacted: Contracts_V0, storage-plan, Multi-Account, Prompt_Pipeline, Runtime_Artifacts_Panel, usage-feature; UI Orchestrator_Page, Run_Graph_View

Orchestrator_Page weak worker row without execution_role or operational target; usage-feature no execution-role disclosure; Runtime_Artifacts_Panel lacks normalized operational-identity family; provider/account snapshots risk becoming dump for non-provider identity

execution_role in canonical attempt packet Contracts_V0 and storage-plan; operational_identity optional family for receipts/artifacts/side-effect records; worker surfaces show execution role, requested/effective runtime identity, operational target when relevant; usage shared schema with execution-role display/filter

Do-not-forget execution_role vs operational_identity: different problems, not merged; provider/account shared-runtime truth; operational identity side-effect/target truth; strongest anchor for operational_identity is receipt/bridge not persona snapshot
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Sonnet owner-doc tranche synthesis

Sonnet tranche targeted docs: Commands_System, Wiring_Matrix, UI_Wiring_Rules, Project_Output_Artifacts, Glossary, FileManager, Crosswalk, Decision_Policy, Run_Modes, Progression_Gates, newtools, assistant-memory-subsystem

Artifact/runtime-observability gap cluster: validation_pass_report.pass_verdict vs skipped; project artifact events under-keyed vs EventRecord; glossary/evidence artifact types unregistered; FileManager OpenFile path-only vs open-by-identity addendum; newtools uncataloged preview/build cmds, live.*, doctor/custom-headless, CustomHeadlessTool without Tools owner; assistant-memory memory.gist.* without storage registration, AutoRunBoundary/AutoMilestone without lifecycle events, handoff actions without cmd.*

Glossary/Crosswalk structurally unsafe: Overseer cited §2 missing; attempt/attempt_id, safe point, lane, work package no Glossary owner; effective state wording shadows requested/effective execution model; Crosswalk duplicate numbering, wrong ContractRef, missing §2 index, orphaned surfaces; rewrite primitives (Seglog, evidence-bundle, capability gating) unroutable

Decision_Policy/Run_Modes/Progression_Gates: missing startup-recovery defaults, retry ceiling collision with prohibited derived fields, backoff/manual/prerequisite resume unowned; Contribute(PR) vs DAE isolation, DAE-jail durability, yolo step ambiguity, external_publish_side_effect in DAE, mid-run account-switch strategy invalidation unresolved; Progression_Gates duplicate addenda, unnumbered runtime gates, GATE-007/008 placeholders, GATE-012 collapses attention_required and true wizard blocked; attention_required persistence unverifiable — storage/event family unowned

Primary owners listed: Commands_System, Wiring_Matrix, UI_Wiring_Rules, Project_Output_Artifacts, Glossary, FileManager, Crosswalk, Decision_Policy, Run_Modes, Progression_Gates, newtools, assistant-memory-subsystem; cross-owner: UI_Command_Catalog, Contracts_V0, storage-plan, assistant-chat-design, Orchestrator_Page, Executor_Protocol, WorktreeGitImprovement, Multi-Account

Ghost/stale IDs survive without tombstone model; mutation/recovery depends on preconditions wiring/gates cannot express; artifact lineage needs anchors project artifacts underspecify; no coherent owner for rewrite operational nouns (Overseer, attempt, Seglog, promotions, handoff kinds); gates vs addendum prose splits mandatory checks from registry

Register/fix command families, retire false claims; extend wiring/gates for runtime gating machine-verifiable; promote artifact/memory/live records to full owner status; repair Glossary/Crosswalk structure; close governance gaps in policy/run-mode/gate docs explicitly

Do-not-forget Sonnet tranche: owner docs make false/unverifiable claims; pattern is runtime concepts exist but registration/verification owners lag; highest-risk for continuation Commands_System, Wiring_Matrix, UI_Wiring_Rules, Project_Output_Artifacts, FileManager, Decision_Policy, Run_Modes, Progression_Gates, newtools, assistant-memory, plus Glossary/Crosswalk SSOT failures

Tool events, artifacts, receipts, usage want shared attribution but docs separate worlds: Tools.md tool.invoked analytics-light; Runtime_Artifacts_Panel artifact-centric ID set; storage-plan strongest (attempt_record provider_attempt_ref, orchestrator.receipt bridge, usage_record lineage); Contracts_V0 tightens tool.denied when scheduler affected but tool.invoked and runtime-artifact docs lag
